pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Healing the Blind — a bald old man in a grey blue robe groping forward with both hands open while a close press of bearded heads crowds in behind his shoulder and a woman in rose and gold turns away in the foreground before a white classical temple and a far street, when jesus had finished saying these things, he left galilee and went into the region of judea beyond the jordan, large crowds followed him, and he healed them there

pictures.scene: Dirck van Delen, The Pharisee and the Publican — a vast pale church interior of tall columns and a blue and cream chequered floor with a Pharisee in a dark red cloak standing at the left with one hand raised and his face lifted while a publican in a red robe stands far off at the right with his head bowed and both hands on his breast, then some pharisees came and tested him by asking, is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason, jesus answered, have you not read that from the beginning the creator made them male and female

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Peasant Wedding — a barn wedding feast where a man in a blue jacket and a white apron carries a plank of porridge bowls across the floor while another in a red cap lifts the bowls off it and the bride sits still under a green hanging cloth with a paper crown above her head and the guests eat and drink along the bench, and said, for this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh, so they are no longer two, but one flesh, therefore what god has joined together, let man not separate

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Moses Smashing the Tablets of the Law — a grey bearded Moses in a pale robe lifting the dark stone tablet of Hebrew letters high above his head with both hands, his face raised and lit against a bare brown hillside, and a red sash at his waist, why then, they asked, did moses order a man to give his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away, jesus replied, moses permitted you to divorce your wives because of your hardness of heart, but it was not this way from the beginning

pictures.scene: Quentin Metsys, The Moneylender and His Wife — a man in a black fur cap weighing a small gold coin on a balance over a table of coins and pearls while his wife in a scarlet gown and white headdress turns from her illuminated book to watch the scales, a round convex mirror lying on the board between them, now i tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman, commits adultery, his disciples said to him, if this is the case between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry

pictures.scene: Antonello da Messina, Saint Jerome in His Study — a scholar in a red robe and red cap sitting alone at a wooden study platform reading an open book inside a vast arched hall of shelves and pots, his slippers set down on the tiled floor and a peacock and a partridge standing on the step in front, not everyone can accept this word, he replied, but only those to whom it has been given, for there are eunuchs who were born that way, others were made that way by men, and still others live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven, the one who can accept this should accept it

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jacob Blessing the Sons of Joseph — a white haired Jacob propped up on a red bed laying his open hand on the fair head of a kneeling boy while a second dark haired child looks out beside him and Joseph in a pale turban reaches across to steady his father's arm, then the little children were brought to jesus for him to place his hands on them and pray for them, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them, but jesus said, let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these

pictures.scene: Duccio, Christ and the Samaritan Woman — Christ in a red tunic and a blue mantle seated on the rim of a hexagonal well with one hand raised in speech while a woman in cream robes stands across from him with a clay jar balanced on her head and her hand lifted in answer, all against a worn gold ground, and after he had placed his hands on them, he went on from there, just then a man came up to jesus and inquired, teacher, what good thing must i do to obtain eternal life

pictures.scene: Philippe de Champaigne, Moses with the Ten Commandments — a white bearded Moses in a blue robe and a gold embroidered mantle, two small rays rising from his hair, holding up a tall stone tablet lettered with the commandments and resting one worn hand on the ledge in front of him, why do you ask me about what is good, jesus replied, there is only one who is good, if you want to enter life, keep the commandments, which ones, the man asked, jesus answered, do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness
pictures.name: pd_champaigne_moses_with_the_ten_commandments

pictures.scene: Jan Steen, Prayer Before the Meal — a mother in a white cap sitting by an open window with her baby on her lap and her head bowed while the father prays with folded hands across the table and a child's dark head rests against him, a loaf of bread and a cheese on the white cloth and a written panel hanging on the wall behind, honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself, all these i have kept, said the young man, what do i still lack
pictures.name: pd_steen_prayer_before_the_meal

pictures.scene: Heinrich Hofmann, Christ and the Rich Young Ruler — Christ in a dark red robe and a blue mantle with one hand open in appeal and a young man in a jewelled turban and a cream cloak over green silk standing at his right with his eyes lowered and his face troubled, a plain stone wall behind them both, jesus told him, if you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven, then come, follow me, when the young man heard this, he went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth
pictures.name: pd_hofmann_christ_and_the_rich_young_ruler

pictures.scene: James Tissot, The Caravan — a long train of laden camels and white robed riders winding down a tawny desert valley in watercolour, the nearest beast harnessed in red and blue and carrying a rider wrapped in a white burnous, with small walking figures scattered over the slopes beyond, then jesus said to his disciples, truly i tell you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven, again i tell you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of god
pictures.name: pd_tissot_caravan

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Christ in Glory — Christ robed in pale blue and enthroned inside a deep blue mandorla ringed with small cherub heads, one hand raised in blessing on a burnished gold ground, with the Virgin and crowned saints kneeling on clouds at either side and a winged angel holding the cross below, when the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and asked, who then can be saved, jesus looked at them and said, with man this is impossible, but with god all things are possible
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_christ_in_glory

pictures.scene: Eugene Burnand, The Disciples Peter and John Running to the Tomb — two men running side by side in sepia, the younger in a pale cloak with his hands clasped at his breast and his hair blown back, the older grey bearded and wide eyed with his dark cloak streaming behind him, look, peter replied, we have left everything to follow you, what then will there be for us, jesus said to them, truly i tell you, in the renewal of all things, when the son of man sits on his glorious throne, you who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of israel
pictures.name: pd_burnand_disciples_running

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Harvesters — a golden wheat field under a spreading pear tree where reapers sit in its shade eating bread and porridge and drinking from a jug while one man lies sprawled asleep against the trunk, sheaves standing in rows across the stubble and a village spire among the trees beyond, and everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of my name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life, but many who are first will be last, and the last will be first
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_harvesters

lines.text: When Jesus had finished saying these things, He left Galilee and went into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.
Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them there.
Then some Pharisees came and tested Him by asking, Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?
Jesus answered, Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator made them male and female,
and said, For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh?
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.
Why then, they asked, did Moses order a man to give his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away?
Jesus replied, Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because of your hardness of heart; but it was not this way from the beginning.
Now I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman, commits adultery.
His disciples said to Him, If this is the case between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry.
Not everyone can accept this word, He replied, but only those to whom it has been given.
For there are eunuchs who were born that way; others were made that way by men; and still others live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who can accept this should accept it.
Then the little children were brought to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them and pray for them. And the disciples rebuked those who brought them.
But Jesus said, Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.
And after He had placed His hands on them, He went on from there.
Just then a man came up to Jesus and inquired, Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?
Why do you ask Me about what is good? Jesus replied. There is only One who is good. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.
Which ones? the man asked. Jesus answered, Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness,
honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.
All these I have kept, said the young man. What do I still lack?
Jesus told him, If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.
When the young man heard this, he went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.
Then Jesus said to His disciples, Truly I tell you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.
Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and asked, Who then can be saved?
Jesus looked at them and said, With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.
Look, Peter replied, we have left everything to follow You. What then will there be for us?

Jesus said to them, Truly I tell you, in the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of My name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.
